messages:
maya: Heads-up — we need to onboard end-to-end correlation metrics for the new runtime dashboards. Proposal: standardize a request-id header and deterministic sampling. Need infra + metrics + console signoff. Who's in?

jonathan: +1. Deterministic sampling sounds right so sampled set is stable across services. Can we do hash(req_id) % 100 < sample_pct?

kevin: yep — simple and reliable. Example: `sampled = (fnv1a(req_id) % 100) < sample_pct`

lisa: note: we already pass `traceparent` for full traces. Are we inventing another header or reusing `x-request-id`?

maya: thinking `x-redwood-req-id` to avoid collisions with upstream proxies and make intent explicit. Also add a top-level `x-redwood-sampled: 1/0` set by the entrypoint so downstream knows whether to keep spans.

kevin: +1 to `x-redwood-req-id`. Important: do NOT add req_id as a Prometheus label (high-card). We'll keep req_id in logs/traces and use aggregate labels for metrics.

infra-bot: deploy plan draft: feature-flag `correlation.metrics.v1` to gate header passthrough + sampler. Export schema v1: topic `redwood.correlation.events` with keys: `req_id`, `trace_id`(opt), `sampled`, `route`, `model`, `region`, `latency_ms`, `status_code`.

lisa: for dashboards we need these aggregates: request_rate(route,model), sampled_trace_rate, latency_p50/p95 (aggregate + sampled), and a missing-reqid counter. Also add alert when sampled_trace_rate deviates >20% from expected.

jonathan: sampling policy details: default global 1% deterministic. Allow per-tenant override (tenant metadata) and higher rate for canaries (10%). Implementation: `hash(req_id) % 10000 < tenant_rate*100` so we get 2-decimal precision.

kevin: metrics team — design queries to compute sampling drift. Eg: `sum(rate(correlation_events_total{sampled="1"}[5m])) / sum(rate(correlation_events_total[5m]))` and compare to configured rate.

product-nora: UX note: Console should show an opt-in toggle for tenants, and for tenants opted-in show a sample badge next to request rows with a link "open trace" when available. Also show an admin view of sampling coverage.

maya: privacy: we must strip PII from correlation events. The event schema above should not include headers or payloads. Confirm?

lisa: confirmed — no bodies or headers beyond the req-id and route/model tags. We'll redact any param values that look like emails/ids before sending.

kevin: implementation constraints: runtime to set `x-redwood-req-id` if missing, propagate across gRPC/http, add `x-redwood-span-id` for root span so Tempo can link quickly. Also emit `x-redwood-sampled` header.

jonathan: I'll open the runtime PR for header passthrough + deterministic sampler today (will include code snippet):
```
// pseudo
req_id = getOrSetHeader(req, "x-redwood-req-id")
sampled = (fnv1a(req_id) % 10000) < tenant_rate*100
setHeader(req, "x-redwood-sampled", sampled ? "1" : "0")
```

maya: infra action items: create Kafka topic + schema, docs for sample-rate per-tenant, and a migration plan for feature-flag rollout. Metrics: draft dashboard queries and alerts. Console: add trace-linker and tenant toggle. Runtime: PR + tests.

kevin: one more callout — do not use req_id as a metric label. For trace links we can store trace_id in the event and UI link directly to traces by trace_id.

product-nora: can we show sample percent in tenant settings UI and a small explainer about costs / privacy? yes please.

maya: perfect. I'm scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow 11am PT to walk the plan and map owners. Tagging infra + metrics + console: @kevin @lisa @jonathan @product-nora. :calendar:

deploy-bot: FYI — feature-flag `correlation.metrics.v1` created in staging; rollout to prod gated on infra + runtime PRs merged.
